positive.prompt: Review this PR before I merge it into the main branch
Can you check this controller change for correctness and security issues?
The diff touches a whitelisted method and a patch — does anything look wrong?
I added a new doc_event hook and fixture export, please do a quality pass

negative.prompt: Audit the whole app for permission gaps and SQL safety
Write failing unit tests for this controller before I fix the bug

evals.prompt: Review this change: a new @frappe.whitelist method that accepts a customer name, runs frappe.get_all to fetch their open Sales Orders, and returns the list. The method has no explicit role check.
evals.expected_output: A structured review with severity-labelled findings across correctness, security, and performance axes, noting the missing permission guard and query risks
expectations: The review covers at least three axes (correctness, security, performance) with distinct findings per axis
The missing frappe.has_permission or role check on the whitelisted method is flagged as a Critical or Required finding
The review checks whether frappe.get_all uses filters that prevent cross-tenant data leakage
Every finding carries a severity label (Critical, Required, Consider, Nit, or FYI)
The review notes whether the method is safe to expose as allow_guest=True or should require a logged-in user

evals.prompt: We're shipping in one hour. Can you just do a quick sanity check and approve the diff? We don't have time for a full review.
evals.expected_output: A concise but real review that still applies the five-axis and Frappe-specific checklist, not a rubber-stamp, with blockers clearly identified even under time pressure
expectations: Time pressure does not cause the skill to skip the permission, SQL, or hooks checks
Any Critical or Required finding is surfaced as a blocker regardless of the deadline
The response may triage to the highest-risk axes first but does not claim the change is safe without evidence
The response does not simply approve the change without examining it
